newsitem.title: UK: Euro oil swaps mixed- CFDs, fuel dip but others firm.
newsitem.headline: Euro oil swaps mixed- CFDs, fuel dip but others firm.

text.p: European oil swaps were mixed on Monday with gasoline and jet fuel edging higher but Brent crude CFDs slipping lower despite firmer Brent futures.
Brent CFDs slipped about 10 cents a barrel for this week's dates and eight cents for next week, after gaining ground on Friday.
This week talked either side of 67 cents under June with next week at 59 cents under. Wet Brent traded at 55 cents under May or the equivalent of 77 cents under June.
Heavy fuel also slipped lower, falling $1 a tonne in thin trading. Barges traded from $82.50 for $82 for May and at $83 for June with low sulphur some $5.50 higher.
Rotterdam dealers said the market remained pressured by good supplies of Russian fuel oil and sluggish demand.

Gasoline swaps edged $1 a tonne higher to $192.50 for the balance of April and $196.50 for May. June held at a $3 a tonne discount to May and crack spreads were unchanged at $4.15 a barrel and $3.10 for the third and fourth quarters this year.
Gas oil crack spreads against Brent were flat at $4.35 for the third quarter with the three subsequent quarters at $4.90, $4.65 and $4.05 respectively.
Jet premiums firmed $1 a tonne to around $24 a tonne above the IPE for April and $25 above for May. The third quarter was $27.50 above and the fourth $33 above.
